Expected Information of a Multivariate Distribution, by Sampling

Source: R/multivariate.R
distrib_expected_hessian.multivariate_distrib.Rd

Computes the expected information of a multivariate family without a closed form as an average over a sample drawn from the family. Every shipped multivariate class registers its own closed form, so this method runs only for a family written elsewhere.

Arguments

distrib

A multivariate_distrib() object without a closed form of its own.

y

An \(n \times p\) numeric matrix of observations; only its row count is used, because the expectation is over the law.

theta

A named list of parameters, in which each component is a single number.

scale

One of "parameter" (the default) or "link". The generic applies the link scale to the result of the method.

method

NULL (the default), which selects expect_opg(), or an object inheriting from ExpectMethod. expect_opg() and expect_mc() sample, and expect_integrate() signals an error. See expected_derivative_methods.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors of length \(n\), keyed as hess_names(distrib@params), in which each vector is constant.

The routes

The "integrate" route of continuous_distrib() splits a one-dimensional integral at quantiles, and a multivariate family has no quantiles, so method = expect_integrate() signals an error. The other methods sample: expect_opg() and expect_mc() with identity = "score" average the negative outer product of the score over simulated draws, and expect_mc() with identity = "hessian" averages the observed Hessian. The two averages agree in expectation by the second Bartlett identity and differ by sampling error at any finite nsim. The sample size is that of expect_mc() and 10000 for expect_opg(). The routine mv_expected_sampled() does the sampling and also serves an explicit method for a multivariate family that has a closed form.

Monte Carlo error

The result carries Monte Carlo error of order nsim^(-1/2), and two calls under different seeds give different values. A seed set before the call makes the result reproducible, and a fit that inverts this matrix moves with it.

See also

distrib_expected_hessian.MvGaussianDistrib() and distrib_expected_hessian.MvStudentTDistrib() for two closed forms, expected_hessian_exact(), which reports whether a family has a closed form, and distrib_expected_hessian() for the generic.

Examples

# Every shipped family has its own method, so the fallback is called
# directly.
d <- mvgaussian1_distrib(2)
theta <- list(mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, sigma_log_L1 = 0, sigma_log_L2 = 0,
              sigma_L2.1 = 0.5)
base <- S7::method(distrib_expected_hessian, multivariate_distrib)

set.seed(1)
sampled <- base(d, matrix(0, 3, 2), distributions7:::align_theta(d, theta),
                method = expect_mc(nsim = 4000))
exact <- distrib_expected_hessian(d, matrix(0, 3, 2), theta)
round(rbind(sampled = vapply(sampled, function(z) z[1], numeric(1)),
            closed = vapply(exact, function(z) z[1], numeric(1))), 3)
#>         mu1_mu1 mu2_mu2 sigma_log_L1_sigma_log_L1 sigma_log_L2_sigma_log_L2
#> sampled   -1.25      -1                    -2.415                    -2.008
#> closed    -1.25      -1                    -2.250                    -2.000
#>         sigma_L2.1_sigma_L2.1 mu1_mu2 mu1_sigma_log_L1 mu1_sigma_log_L2
#> sampled                -1.073     0.5           -0.009           -0.014
#> closed                 -1.000     0.5            0.000            0.000
#>         mu1_sigma_L2.1 mu2_sigma_log_L1 mu2_sigma_log_L2 mu2_sigma_L2.1
#> sampled          0.015            0.001            0.028         -0.001
#> closed           0.000            0.000            0.000          0.000
#>         sigma_log_L1_sigma_log_L2 sigma_log_L1_sigma_L2.1
#> sampled                    -0.003                   0.539
#> closed                      0.000                   0.500
#>         sigma_log_L2_sigma_L2.1
#> sampled                   0.006
#> closed                    0.000

# Two seeds give two values, because the result is a sample.
set.seed(2)
again <- base(d, matrix(0, 3, 2), distributions7:::align_theta(d, theta),
              method = expect_mc(nsim = 4000))
c(first = sampled$mu1_mu1[1], second = again$mu1_mu1[1])
#>  first second 
#>  -1.25  -1.25
